In every company, this happens. We are talking about book-entries. Simple schedule:

  1. Buying

To be received: 100 on the debet side of the books against

Accounts payable on the credit side.

  1. Receipt of goods

Entry in Ware House 70 on de debet side

Applicable sales Tax to be paid 30 on the debit side.

Invoice to be received 100 on the credit side

As you can see, every line item in the bookingsystem needs to be related to the other. Invoicenumber, ordernumber, article number a lot. Multiply these entries with a 100 million and you'll soon see what is going on. With current workflow systems these issues missing/ misattribution can be decreased.

Now multiply the amount of warehouses with 10.000 and you'll also see that a new qualifier comes into play: warehouse number, and the exact location of that particular item. With another number: barcode, an item can be followed. However, this does not negate transport issues. Within transport, a lot gets misplaced, despite track and trace. First outright theft, falling of the truck, falling of the transport band, whatever. And it is not only small items, as pens. A logistics company I worked for, a chem company I investigated lost dozens upon dozens of barrels with cleaning fluid during transport. And sometimes it is inoccuous: like an accident on the road, where a truck capsizes, or a container gets blown of a ship.

The last section of book entries in Accounts payable is payment.

usually, payment is only executed after authorisation. With workflow management, from order to payment the column can be followed. However, with the previous info in mind, a lot can still go wrong. For a company I worked for, and this is only small potatoes, in a 3 year period on a 100 million turnover, I identified 3 million in non-applied payments, meaning, a payment had been done, but no invoice could be booked against that payment.

It also means , the receiving company, receives monies for invoices already paid. Usually, this money is set "aside", and accrued on a special book-account. Once every year, this account is cleaned. It is not uncommon for a company to add 10.000 a year to it's coffers due to non-applied payments. The loss of the one, is the profit of the other. And as long as on a particular level of a company, these monies are not material, it simply vanishes.

Another level on which things go wrong is a company receives an order, processes it, sends the goods, but .... the invoice, though send and received, is not scanned into the workflow management system, due to scanning errors. However, once an invoicenumber has been occupied in the system, it cannot be used again on the same Accounts Payable account, so the invoicenumber needs amending. This is where things go off the rails. With integration, this can be reduced hugely. Since the '90 we have been working and expanding on EDI for instance, for invoices, for booking entries. Basware one, as an example, pertains to reduce these errors to allow an issuing company to directly infuse the contracting parties bookentry with data, pertaining to the contract.
